correctness.rationale: The two mixed Dirichlet–Neumann and the Dirichlet–Dirichlet boundary problems give the three stated transforms. Setting kappa=sqrt(r/D), the relevant distances in units of 1/kappa are s-delta, s+delta, and s to the midpoint, with s=(L/2)kappa. On substituting r+u*theta_r, the relative wavenumber change is O(exp(-s)), and its product with the largest scaled distance is O(s exp(-s))=o(1). Thus the three one-cycle success transforms times exp(s) tend to a=e^delta, b=e^(-delta), and a+b, respectively. Renewal produces the three exponential survivor limits with these rates; exact retained-history inclusion–exclusion gives the maximum law, with no finite-rate independence assumption. For 0<epsilon<min(a,b), the failed-cycle weight at the positive exponential tilt is r(1-F(r-epsilon*theta_r))/(r-epsilon*theta_r)<1 for each endpoint by the same transform estimates. Summing the convergent geometric series bounds each tilted single-hit moment uniformly, and the cover exponential is at most their sum. This justifies every positive real power. Integrating the limiting survivor gives Gamma(q+1)(a^(-q)+b^(-q)-(a+b)^(-q)), including the displayed mean, second moment and symmetric variance/CV. The initial site is interior for all sufficiently large r at fixed delta. The frozen checker was read, not executed, and the review relies on the exact renewal and moment arguments.

originality.rationale: No new finite-rate transform or midpoint claim survives this comparison: the earlier all-site variance record already gives the three exact transforms and arbitrary-site cover-survival resolvent when combined by inclusion–exclusion; the exact arbitrary-site mean and the exact midpoint law are also prior. The assessed result is the full moving-site distributional crossover together with moment convergence on the natural competition scale. At fixed nonzero detuning in that scale the two excursion probabilities remain comparable, so the one-farthest-target simplification does not apply. The claimed limit requires the joint wavenumber/frequency asymptotics in the known resolvent, and the tilted renewal bound is a separate uniform-in-r step. value.rationale: The diffusive displacement in a reset interval sets the unique natural order of location detuning for which the two exponentially rare endpoint probabilities remain comparable. The limiting maximum law clarifies the transition where a single-farthest-target approximation misses the cover-time distribution, and the proven moment convergence gives meaningful risk measures on that same scale. This is not a claim of exact finite-rate clock independence or of uniformity for unbounded detuning.
